analysis:
This batch contains only changelog.d markdown files and docs/architecture/inference.md. No executable source was supplied, so every claim about code behavior is unverified. The changelogs describe: (1) bounded-memory hashing in provider updates; (2) CI memory sampling (report-only); (3) Gemma tensor-parallel build-ahead for greedy and sampled requests; (4) metal-cpp taken from the sandbox image, pinned by SHA-256; (5) Qwen3.8-27B public speculative assistant; (6) Qwen TP decode layer stride of 8.

Security-relevant points for later passes, none of them findings from this evidence:
- The Qwen27 public assistant (inference.md, head lines ~7444-7454; changelog qwen27-public-assistant.md) changes what a coordinator-formed pair computes. The doc says the assistant digest and the declared settings are folded into the resource policy digest (`DistributedInstalledNativeStart.resourcePolicySHA256`), approval validation refuses a mismatched assistant before any part stops, and the parity qualification rests on an evidence report. Integration should check that code enforces this. This relates to T-054 and TB-011 (qualification and approval binding) and T-056, which warns against overclaiming correctness. The doc itself says tiny fixtures do not establish the evidence. The claim is based on one pair and a report outside this batch.
- Speed records now carry `serving` and `tensorAssistant` scope. This affects planning only. No trust impact is visible.
- Gemma build-ahead means a rank's stop rides one step later, so rank 0 may stream one extra token before the request errors on both ranks. The change notes it is the same as GLM and the token count is dropped. This is a minor availability or accuracy nuance, not a confidentiality issue. The tokens are still answered to the owner and sealed per the existing path. T-008 and T-010 (cancellation and encryption failing closed) cannot be confirmed from docs alone.
- The metal-cpp change to scripts/fetch-metallib.sh is a build-supply-chain item. It is described as using the image archive only when the SHA-256 matches the pin, which is a sound control, but the script itself was not supplied and needs review.
- Build-ahead for Qwen is documented as not on in the product (`buildsAhead` false), so there is no new runtime surface yet.

No prompt, key, attestation or authorization behavior is changed in the supplied text, and I identified no regression or threat-model invalidation. Further review of the underlying Swift and script changes is recommended.
